errors.english: For those who are not already suffering, sufferings only increase further.
errors.why: The Tibetan (Skt. vyasaneṣv eva) says suffering increases precisely for those already suffering; the English adds a negation.

fix.find: For those who are not already suffering
fix.replace: For those who are already suffering

errors.english: With his unbearable scepter of punishment [note: or taxes] and by seizing the property of all
errors.why: The line comparing the king to untimely death (Skt. akālakālakalpena) is not rendered.

errors.english: Being tormented by intense heat, the clouds did not send down rain.
errors.why: It is the people scorched by intense heat on whom the clouds did not rain, not the clouds that are tormented.

note: Good rendering of the verse narrative, but one inverted line about suffering and a missed simile.
Faithful rendering of a technical momentariness argument, including the variant-reading remark.

errors.english: the city ends mid-sentence
errors.why: The Tibetan just reads 'the city' as the sentence continues on the next side; 'ends mid-sentence' is a leaked translator's remark.

errors.english: For the sake of illustration
errors.why: The Buddha spoke making clear the excellence of giving (sbyin pa khyad 'phags); the subject of the illustration is lost.

errors.english: the Noble Sena [note: original: Shrisena]
errors.why: dpal gyi sde is the proper name Śrīsena; dpal is Śrī, not 'Noble'.

errors.english: the Jewel among Men born for the sake of the world's happiness
errors.why: bde bar 'gro ba renders sugati/sugata (Skt. prakaṭitasugatiḥ, one who manifests the Sugata's path), not 'the world's happiness'.

note: Readable rendering of the colophon and opening verses, with a leaked meta-remark and loosened names and terms.

errors.english: From imputation, the fire of the limbs arises
errors.why: Likely yan lag med = Anaṅga (Kāma): from imagining arises the fire of the Bodiless One, not 'fire of the limbs'.

errors.english: Wrapping themselves around women is like embracing a blazing, spark-strewn fire born of iron.
errors.why: The Tibetan describes the hell torment of embracing a blazing iron woman covered in sparks, not a simile for embracing women.

note: Difficult kāvya on desire rendered sensibly overall; a few images are loosened.

errors.english: are in no way existent entities, because they are not observed in any way whatsoever
errors.why: ji ltar yang renders kathaṃcit, 'in some respect' (the Jaina syādvāda example): self, pot etc. are in some respect non-existent because in some respect not apprehended.

fix.find: are in no way existent entities, because they are not observed in any way whatsoever
fix.replace: are in some respect non-existent in nature, because in some respect they are not observed

errors.english: are in every way of an existent nature, because they are observed in any way whatsoever
errors.why: Again kathaṃcit: the hare's horn is in some respect existent because in some respect apprehended, not existent 'in every way'.

fix.find: are in every way of an existent nature, because they are observed in any way whatsoever
fix.replace: are in some respect existent in nature, because in some respect they are observed

errors.english: This is because it is observed in any manner whatsoever, whether as a real entity or a non-entity.
errors.why: This is a sample inference with a single-characteristic reason ('entity or non-entity is existent in nature, because in some respect apprehended'), not a justification of the preceding claim; 'existent in nature' is dropped.

fix.find: This is because it is observed in any manner whatsoever, whether as a real entity or a non-entity.
fix.replace: For example: "Entity or non-entity is existent in nature, because it is in some respect observed."

note: The anyathānupapatti argument is followed, but the Jaina 'in some respect' (kathaṃcit) examples are systematically misread.
Accurate rendering of a dense non-apprehension (anupalabdhi) commentary.

errors.english: the diverse elements do not gather into the (avayavin) the whole
errors.why: 'du ba here is the Vaiśeṣika category inherence (samavāya): variegatedness does not inhere in the whole; 'gather into' loses the technical sense throughout the passage.

fix.find: the diverse elements do not gather into the (avayavin) the whole
fix.replace: variegatedness does not inhere in the (avayavin) the whole

errors.english: The threads and so forth, each of which is possessed by the gathering, also become like that; they are not inherently diverse in themselves.
errors.why: The threads, by inherence in which [the whole] would become so, are each not variegated; the English says the threads 'also become like that', which contradicts the point.

errors.english: On the other hand, how is fire perceived as fire?
errors.why: This opens an opponent's analogy ('Objection: just as, having grasped fire as fire...'), not a question.

note: The citra-rūpa debate is broadly tracked, but the inherence terminology and the objection's framing are blurred.

errors.english: > Actions differentiated by virtue and so forth are likewise of two kinds.
errors.why: This is the commentator's prose lead-in, not a line of the root verse, which begins at dran srong mchog.

note: Faithful rendering of the cetanā/cetayitvā commentary.

errors.english: a living soul, an individual, a person, a human being
errors.why: The list includes gso ba (poṣa, 'nourisher'), which the English drops or misaligns with the following terms.

note: Sound rendering of the path passage and the Akṣayamati quotation.

errors.english: the text cuts off mid-sentence
errors.why: A translator's process remark leaked into the text; the sentence just continues on the next side.

errors.english: sanghadisesa
errors.why: This is a Mūlasarvāstivāda text; the Sanskrit term is saṃghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.

errors.english: "The remaining parts are to be heard as before,"
errors.why: The formula declares the unrecited remainder 'as [already] heard' (śruta), so it is not recited; 'to be heard' suggests it will be recited.

note: Accurate Vinaya procedure with a Pali term and a leaked meta-remark to fix.
